Ladies and gentlemen, it's time to start. Welcome. The 58th plenary meeting of the 10th emergency special session of the General Assembly is called to order. The Assembly will continue its consideration of agenda item five entitled, Illegal Israeli Actions in Occupied East Jerusalem and the Rest of the Occupied Palestinian Territory. I now give the floor to His Excellency Do Hong Viet, Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs of Vietnam.

Mr. President, we are approaching the end of 2024, but we are nowhere near the end of the conflict and the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and across the Middle East. In just over a year, we have witnessed the unfolding of a conflict that has taken the lives of more than 40,000 people. Many are women and children. Nearly two million are being displaced. Infrastructure is systematically obliterated. Schools, hospitals, homes are destroyed in Beit Lahia, in Gaza City, in Rafah, and beyond. Even if the conflict were to end today, according to the UN Conference on Trade and Development, it would take at least three centuries for Gaza's GDP to be restored to the 2022 level. The need to put an end to the suffering of the people in Gaza and pursue lasting peace in the Middle East is paramount. Vietnam continues to call for an immediate, enforceable, and lasting ceasefire across Gaza and the broader region. We also call for the unconditional release of all hostages, many of whom are citizens of ASEAN member states. Vietnam commends the efforts and engagements of several member states over the past year towards this end. Unfortunately, successes have been short-lived while the underlying crisis remains. We are disappointed at the Security Council's failure to act to fulfill its primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. We call on members of the Council to overcome the current deadlock and bring about decisive, comprehensive action to address the multifaceted crisis in Gaza and the broader Middle East. Mr. President, Vietnam condemns the widespread, indiscriminate, and disproportionate attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in violation of the UN Charter and international law. We call for utmost restraint, strict adherence to the UN Charter and international law, and full respect for relevant resolutions of the UN Security Council, the General Assembly, and the provisional measures of the ICJ. Parties must ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure indispensable to the survival of the population. Vietnam calls for more effective measures to ensure unimpeded and uninterrupted humanitarian relief for civilian populations in Gaza and other affected areas in the region. We deeply appreciate the vital work of UNRWA in delivering essential assistance and services to the Palestinian people. We support all efforts to ensure the safe, effective, and continued operation of UNRWA, which include ensuring necessary resources and capabilities for the Agency to carry out their mandates, particularly amid the perilous conditions in Gaza today. Vietnam once again reaffirms its unwavering support for the Palestinian people in exercising their inalienable rights to self-determination and fulfilling the legitimate aspirations for full membership in the United Nations. We strongly advocate for a two-state solution that ensures the establishment of an independent and sovereign state of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders in accordance with international law and relevant UN resolutions. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs of Vietnam. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Malaysia.

Mr. President, thank you for convening this meeting. Malaysia aligns with statements of the Non-Aligned Movement and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. Mr. President, 431 days have passed since Israel's onslaught on Gaza began. Over 44,000 deaths of mostly women and children have been recorded. More than 105,000 have been injured. 2024 has also become the deadliest year on record for humanitarian workers, with 178 killed in the occupied Palestinian territory alone. The humanitarian situation in Gaza has long been described as apocalyptic. Still, humanitarian aid continues to be obstructed. According to OCHA, between 1st and 30th November, the UN attempted to reach besieged areas in North Gaza 53 times, out of which 48 were denied outright. Five were initially approved but then severely impeded on the ground. None was facilitated. The situation now has become unimaginably horrific. Israel's bombings have turned Gaza into a barren wasteland. About 60% of buildings in the strip have been destroyed or damaged, creating about 42 million tons of rubble, which would take decades to clear. Critical infrastructure, including for clean water and sanitation, has been decimated. The damaging environmental impacts of the bombings pose serious risks to the health and well-being of Gazans and will endure for a very long time. The situation in the West Bank also continues to worsen. Alarmingly, some Israeli high-ranking officials have openly advocated for annexation. Israeli settlers are growingly emboldened and have become increasingly violent in their attacks and harassments of Palestinians. Illegal settlements continue to spread, along with evictions and demolitions of Palestinian-owned homes and buildings. Israel's security operations have also intensified, which include airstrikes, shelling, live ammunitions and bulldozers, leading to large numbers of death, injuries and arbitrary detentions of civilians, as well as extensive destruction of homes and infrastructure. Israel has also been unrelenting in its attacks on the United Nations, its officials and agencies. UNRWA, the backbone of the humanitarian support system for millions of Palestinian refugees, has long become a target of Israel's malicious disinformation and smear campaign. Israel's decision to ban UNRWA's operations is condemnable and can only be understood in terms of Israel's longstanding strategy to repudiate the refugee status of Palestinians and their right to return. Mr. President, despite clear evidence of egregious violations of international law by Israel, the international community, particularly the Security Council, has failed to act decisively. The Council's inability to adopt a resolution calling for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire because of the use of veto emboldens Israel to be even more ferocious due to the impunity it continues to enjoy. Malaysia unequivocally condemns Israel's aggression in the occupied Palestinian territory and its offensive in the wider region. We also deplore Israel's ban on UNRWA's operations in the occupied Palestinian territory, which undermines the rights of Palestinian refugees as well as the UN's authority. UNRWA must be defended because its role is essential and irreplaceable. Malaysia therefore urges Member States to support and vote in favour of the two resolutions that are being tabled. The adoption of these resolutions are extremely critical to end the slaughter of innocent civilians, women and children in Gaza and to ensure the continuation of the much needed humanitarian activities in the occupied Palestinian territory. Mr. President, Malaysia also calls for an immediate halt to arms and financial support to Israel. This is vital to stop the massacre of children and other innocent civilians in Gaza. In addition, we believe that the Security Council must adopt a Chapter 7 resolution against Israel for its genocidal war. It is also about time for Member States to seriously consider whether Israel still deserves its seat in the General Assembly. Malaysia supports recent moves to hold Israeli leaders accountable for the war against humanity and war crimes committed against Palestinians. We urge member states to support these measures. We must uphold international law to ensure justice, as failure to act will further erode trust in the multilateral process and lead to the breakdown of international law and global order. Mr. President, 75 years since General Assembly Resolution 1812, the quest for Palestinian statehood remains unfulfilled. Malaysia welcomes the upcoming International Conference on the Question of Palestine next year. It provides the ideal opportunity to implement all relevant UN resolutions towards the full realisation of the self-determination of the Palestinian people. The only way to achieve sustainable peace and stability in the region is by ending Israel's illegal occupation of Palestinian lands and realizing a free and independent state of Palestine according to pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital. Malaysia will continue to be steadfast in its support for the rights of the Palestinians and the creation of a free and independent state of Palestine. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Malaysia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cuba.

Mr.

President, we support the statements made by Uganda on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement and Venezuela on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defence of the UN Charter. The new veto of the United States against a draft resolution on the Palestine question in the Security Council, a draft resolution which received the support of the 14 other members of that body. and was to call for a immediate unconditional and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, that new ceasefire was another piece of evidence that the US government is complicit in the Israeli genocide of the Palestinian people. The Cuban delegation echoes the appeals for this Assembly to speak out firmly and with one voice to hold the genocide once and for all urgently via an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire. The General Assembly must see that this ceasefire puts an end to Israel's illegal policies and practices of colonization in the Palestinian territories. These are practices which have gone on for more than seven decades and have included the Israeli apartheid system in the occupied territories. That resolution was adopted by an overwhelming majority of the international community during the 10th... emergency special session of the JEMAL Assembly held on the 10th of May. Mr. President, Israel, with the complicity and support of the United States Government, is responsible, is the party responsible for the dangerous escalation in the region. We condemn the Israeli army's occupation of the demilitarized strip in the occupied Syrian Golan, established in the separation agreement of 1974, which the UN oversaw. The Israeli army's actions are in flagrant violation of international law, Cuba will never stand idly by and simply witness injustice. The Palestinian cause and that of sister nations of the region will always be able to enjoy our utmost solidarity. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Cuba. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Slovenia.

Mr. President, Gaza doesn't exist anymore. It is destroyed. Palestinians are facing hunger, despair, and death. We have said it before, history is the harshest critic of inaction. And history is being written as we sit here today. It has been a year of misery. Misery of the people in Israel during the Hamas attack on 7 October. Misery of the hostages kept in Gaza and their families and friends waiting for their return in agony. misery of the people in Gaza experiencing violence, displacement, killing, hunger, and the lack of the most basic items for survival. Their suffering and agony continues as we meet today. Despite the sound of alarm bells every step of the way, the collective response system vested primarily in the Security Council has failed again and again. A terrible chapter of our generation's story, one day our history, is being written. Quite frankly, the elected members of the Security Council did not want to be a part of that history. We were elected by the membership of this Assembly with a clear mandate of the primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. Slovenia's Security Council candidature had a clear message: building trust, securing our future. We keep trying to step up to the plate. The elected members of the Council build trust among each other to carry the responsibility together. We acted to secure a different future, a future of peace and prosperity for children and future generations in Palestine and in Israel. Day in, day out, we continue to observe the suffering of the people in the Middle East. We continue to see the evolution of misery that has become a clear threat to international peace and security. We therefore regret the use of the veto on the clear demand for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire in Gaza and the demand for the release of the hostages. Mr. President, if we want to secure a different future for the Palestinian children, we must achieve a ceasefire and an end to the war in Gaza. We must also do everything possible to support the work of UNRWA and its personnel in the field. Firstly, and let me quote the Secretary-General from his recent letters to the General Assembly and to the Security Council, quote, "Because UNRWA is the backbone of the United Nations humanitarian relief operations, providing a lifeline, shelter, and other support for the large majority of the population of nearly 2.3 million in Gaza who have all been affected by the ongoing conflict." End of quote. Secondly, because UNRWA has been key to securing the future of children in Gaza for decades, from their first vaccinations to their first steps in education, all the way to vocational and training centers with continuous psychological support to nurture their well-being, given the difficult circumstances in which they grow up. UNRWA is not indispensable just for their survival in this war. UNRWA is crucial for a chance to build a life worth living in Gaza. It has decades of experience, knowledge, capacities, and trust. We take seriously allegations against UNRWA employees brought forward in January. but point out that the Colonna report has found that UNRWA already has robust procedures and mechanisms to ensure the neutrality of the agency and its staff. We recognize that further improvements could be made, and in this regard, we welcome UNRWA's action plan to implement the report's recommendations. With regard to comments on textbooks used in UNRWA schools made earlier in this hall, I want to quote from the Colonna report. Quote, the chair's assessment is that UNRWA has been responsive to allegations of neutrality breaches and criticism about the textbooks and initiated a range of initiatives to ensure neutrality of its teaching material and the teaching, end of quote. In addition, UNRWA has worked with UNESCO since 2011 to reform curricula and teaching materials. Colleagues, I wish to underline that UNRWA's work is mandated by the UN General Assembly as a promise of a just solution of the Palestinian refugee question. It contributes to the broader efforts towards achieving a two-state solution, which is the only just and sustainable solution for peace and security of both Palestinians and Israelis. UNRWA reflects the historical responsibility of the collective membership of the United Nations. UNRWA is part of the social fabric of its areas of operations. It is a factor of stability. In line with the shared commitments on UNRWA, which enjoys 123 signatories, we reaffirm the vital role of the agency. We repeat our call on the Israeli government not to implement its laws concerning UNRWA. No, there are no alternatives to UNRWA. Mr. President, an agency we established is under threat. It is an agency acting on our behalf, on behalf of the values and principles of this organisation. We need to support it. We are all UNRWA. Today, this Assembly will make two important decisions. It will vote on two resolutions, a demand for a ceasefire in Gaza and support for the mandate of UNRWA. Both far from what this organisation should be offering to Palestinians, yet both with an important message, the world has not forgotten Gaza. There is no reason for this war to continue. We need a ceasefire now. We need to bring hostages home now. Slovenia has co-sponsored both resolutions and intends to vote in favour, and we call on others to do the same. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Slovenia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Algeria.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Today we meet, Mr. President, after the failure of the Security Council once again to adopt a draft resolution that calls for a ceasefire in Gaza that was co-sponsored by the elected members collectively. This effort, of which Algeria was a part, motivated by its conviction of the need to move to rein in the Israeli occupiers and the deep regret for the bloodshed on the in the occupied Palestinian territories particularly in the Gaza Strip that draft which has enjoyed the support of 14 members of the Security Council proves that the immediate and unconditional and lasting ceasefire in Gaza has become a collective objective of the international group despite some voices that continue to accept the discourse of the occupiers. Now with the second year of the attack and the aggression against the Palestinian people, the international community continues, regrettably, to enforce its will and to force Israel to cease-fire and to allow humanitarian assistance to arrive at a time when the Gaza Strip is witnessing one of the worst humanitarian tragedies in the modern era. It is a crime of ethnic cleansing and genocide that is happening before our eyes. It's a blemish on the conscience of humanity. We must all ensure the accountability of those responsible for war crimes in Gaza and to facilitate the work of the relevant international organizations and not to impede its work. This is the only way to ensure the continuation of the international system based on the rule of law. Our president, Abdel Majid Tabun said, and I quote, the price of silence and failure in the face of the Palestinian tragedy is a very heavy price and it will be heavier tomorrow. The failure of the international community to impose the international will on Israel does not only threaten the rules of the international system established by our founding fathers and strengthened by successive generations, it also leads to a chaotic system that will be based only on the logic of force and will destroy the balance of justice and law." The international reports and the reports of NGOs and civil society organizations are all Alerting us to a tragedy that is unfolding and is happening, the situation in Gaza, despite its grimness, can be exasperated and can deteriorate because of the blockade of Gaza. population of the Strip are losing hope after the displacement that forced them to keep going around a very small area of land where they cannot enjoy security, peace, or even a crust of bread. The international organizations, despite all their efforts, are suspending their activities because of the lack of response of the Israeli occupiers with their need. and the deliberate targeting of their convoys. In view of the, in this tragic situation, the Israeli authorities took its decision to suspend the activities of UNRWA in the occupied Palestinian territories, thus leading to a further exasperation of the tragedy of the Palestinians. We stress that UNRWA has always been the backbone of the humanitarian in Gaza, no organization, no group of organizations can replace it in fulfilling its mandate for the service of the Palestinian refugees and the civilians who are in dire need of humanitarian assistance. UNRWA was established by a mandate of the General Assembly, which expresses the international will This mandate cannot be touched until and unless the General Assembly decides so, or unless the cause for it is eliminated through a final resolution of the tragedy of the Palestinian refugees in accordance with Resolution 194. Palestinians have paid a very heavy price for their freedom. We all must stand side by side with them to allow them to exercise their established and inalienable rights in the establishment of their independent state with its capital in Al-Quds. We will spare no effort in continuing our support for the Palestinian people and their just cause. Thank you for your kind attention.
I thank the distinguished representative of Algeria. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Morocco.

Mr. President, at the outset, I would like to thank you for your response to the request by the OIC, the Arab group, and to resume the tenth emergency. Since the last meeting of the session, the situation in Palestine has exacerbated, in particular in Gaza, which calls on the international community to take swift and immediate action to stop the war and to compel Israel to lift the siege on the Gaza Strip and allow the refugees and IDPs to return within a process of reconstruction after the destruction made by the war. King Mohammed VI, in his message of solidarity this year addressed to the president of the Committee on the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People, he stated, and I quote, "It is important to reach an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza and to put an end to the repeated attacks against the safe civilians in Gaza Strip and the West Bank. Second, no attack to take place against the civilians in the entire Palestinian territory. Third, it is important to open all crossings in an immediate and permanent manner without any conditions to ensure that humanitarian and relief aid are delivered as well as medical supplies in a smooth, adequate manner and at scale to Palestinians in Gaza and the entire Palestinian territory. Fourth, the role of UNRWA should be maintained. and promoted and supported. Fifth, forced displacement of Palestinians should be rejected and international law and international humanitarian law should be strongly upheld. Sixth, serious negotiations should be relaunched in line with resolutions of the United Nations. End of quote. Therefore, we call to support the resolution submitted today. The first draft resolution calls for an immediate, permanent, unconditional ceasefire to be respected by all parties. The second draft calls for the support of the role of UNRWA. Mr. President, the continued unilateral measures by Israel in Al-Quds Al-Sharif, leads to extremist tensions, violence, and they undermine all efforts for de-escalation. His Majesty King Mohammed Al-Saad, being the chair of the Al-Quds Committee of the OIC, he has been closely following all developments of the Palestinian cause. He spared no effort and invested all tools available to maintain the legal, historic and demographic character of the sacred city, which has significance for the followers of the three monolithic religions. Mr. President, Morocco stresses its firm position about the centrality of the Palestinian cause as key to stability, security, and peace in the Middle East, in line with a two-state solution that would lead to an independent state of Palestine along the borders of 1967, with East Jerusalem as its capital. In conclusion, Mr. President, the Kingdom of Morocco, under the leadership of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, supports the territorial integrity of Lebanon. Morocco believes that the ceasefire announced in Lebanon is a positive step, but it has to be respected and built upon to maintain the integrity, unity and unity of this country. Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Morocco. I will now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Mexico.

That resolution called for a permanent ceasefire, the immediate release of the hostages, and the immediate access of the civilians in the Gaza Strip to basic services and to humanitarian aid. It is estimated that 1.9 million people, 90% of the population, have been displaced on the territory in question. In addition, 1.96 million people are facing critical levels of food insecurity. this deplorable situation is far from improving quite on the contrary it is only worsening the Israeli legislation recently passed according to which an attempt is being made to prohibit the activities of the of unwa on Israeli territory is ultimately manifesting itself as the absence of basic humanitarian aid and activities. None of those activities can be replaced by what the Israeli authorities can do. We must be frank. UNRWA not only provides protection and assistance to 2.5 million Palestinian refugees in the Gaza Strip, West Bank and East Jerusalem. In times such as these, times where multilateralism as a whole is under threat, a resolution to support UNWRA's mandate, that resolution is indeed being considered here, it is an urgent resolution. Mexico's position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has remained unchanged in various multilateral fora. We have been lucidly clear. My country unequivocally condemns the atrocious attacks perpetrated by Hamas on the 7th of October, 2023, attacks perpetrated against Israeli civilians. However, We repudiate the indiscriminate attacks, the disproportionate, unrelenting attacks that have been visited upon the Palestinian civilians and humanitarian personnel by the Israeli Defense Forces. We're seeing the perpetration of atrocities, and as such, the international community has a moral imperative to take urgent action. We must recall that the foundational charter of this organisation states that the Security Council acts on behalf of all of us in maintaining international peace and security. Faced with the Council's inaction, in the on this file the General Assembly is now obliged to play an increasingly key role in order to guarantee peace and security that responsibility includes one that must be shouldered in the face of grave conflicts the adoption of resolution 10/ L24 on the implementation of the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice on the Israeli policies and practices in the occupied territory is a demonstration of what the General Assembly can achieve in international peace and security we are weighing up the draft resolution to call for a ceasefire in Gaza and this is another occasion upon which the General Assembly can shoulder its responsibilities I also wish to recall that France and Mexico have worked flat out to champion an initiative which aims to restrict the use of the veto specifically in cases which might amount to atrocities, in this case atrocities in Gaza being committed, this organization cannot stand idly by while millions of innocent lives are cut short. Mr. President, Mexico lauds the various diplomatic endeavors whose aim is to bring about the peaceful resolution of disputes and respect for international law. particularly international humanitarian law. With that in mind, we commend the recent ministerial conference to promote a humanitarian response in Gaza that was held under the aegis of Egypt and the UN Secretary-General. My country wishes once more to reaffirm its position. Mexico advocates for the two-state solution. a two-state solution which heeds the legitimate security concerns of Israel and, in turn, allows a viable Palestinian state to be strengthened. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Mexico. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Saudi Arabia.

Thank you, Mr. President. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, Most Merciful, my delegation aligns itself with the statement delivered on behalf of the Arab Group, the OIC, GCC, and NAM. I would like to thank you, Mr. President, for resuming the 10th emergency session after the failure of the Security Council once again to adopt a resolution calling for a ceasefire in Gaza and calls for other humanitarian actions. The situation that has repeated more than once over the last 14 months, with every time the Israeli occupation forces persist in their crimes and exacerbate the humanitarian crisis and expand the scope of the aggression, which undermines multilateralism and places the legitimacy and credibility of the world order at stake with the inability to put an end to the Israeli war machine and with the insistence of some to selectively apply international law and international material law and the charter of the UN. At the time when Saudi Arabia is calling on the international community to take swift action to ceasefire in Gaza and ensure the unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid, it welcomes the ceasefire in Lebanon and condemns the Israeli violations of this agreement. Saudi Arabia commends all international efforts in this regard, wishing that this will lead to the implementation of Security Council Resolution 1701 and maintain the sovereignty, security, and stability of Lebanon with the… with the displaced are returning to their homes in safety and security. My country condemns all the attacks by Israel in the buffer zone in Golan and targeting the Syrian territories, which confirms that Israel insists on violating the rules of international law and undermines the ability of Syria to restore its security, stability and territorial integrity. Saudi Arabia stressed the importance of continuing the delivery of services by UNRWA and calls on the international community to implement the advisory opinion of the ICJ issued on July 19th of 2024. Mr. President, Saudi Arabia believes that peace is the strategic choice for the Middle East. Therefore, it spares no effort in promoting all actions that would lead to just and comprehensive peace. In conclusion, Mr. President, my country will vote in favor of the two draft resolutions before the General Assembly today, and we call upon all peace and good-loving states to vote in favor of those two draft resolutions. I thank the distinguished representative of Saudi Arabia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Portugal.

Mr. President, Excellencies, Portugal appreciates the efforts of the elected members of the Security Council in tabling a draft resolution aimed at putting an end to the ongoing armed conflict in Gaza Strip and at achieving a long-awaited ceasefire. Therefore, we stand before this General Assembly compelled to address the implications of yet another veto cast in the Security Council, this time obstructing action on the humanitarian and security crisis in Gaza. We call on all sides to take all steps necessary to protect civilians, as stipulated in the Security Council Resolution 2573 from 2021. by, and I quote, "distinguish between, on the one hand, civilian population, civilian objects, and all other persons and objects afforded protection, and on the other hand, combatants and military objectives, prohibiting indiscriminate and disproportionate attacks." taking all feasible precautions in planning, deciding, and conducting attacks to avoid and in any event minimize harm to civilians and civilian objects." End of quote. The United Nations is entrusted with the purpose of maintaining international peace and security, if needed by taking effective collective measures and by upholding international law. Yet the Council's inability to act repeatedly, hindered by the misuse of the veto, undermines the international community's trust in multilateralism and our collective capacity to address crises of immense human suffering. Eight vetoes have been cast this year, the highest number since 1989 at the end of the Cold War. This highlights a troubling trend of growing division and inaction in addressing global crises. The draft resolution vetoed on 20 November 2024 sought an immediate and unconditional ceasefire in Gaza, the release of hostages, and access to essential and much needed humanitarian aid. These demands are not mere political aspirations, but moral and legal imperatives. As this situation continues to deteriorate, the inaction of the Security Council leaves civilians bearing the brunt of armed violence. Therefore, Portugal continues to call for an immediate and unconditional ceasefire in Gaza, the immediate and unconditional release of hostages, and the unimpeded flow of humanitarian aid to Gaza. We also call for the full respect and support of UNRWA's mandate as stipulated by this Assembly. For that reason, Portugal will vote in favor of the two resolutions later today. The Palestinian question is a collective responsibility that member states of the United States undertook since the very inception of this organization. However, tensions on the ground rose to historic heights during 2022 and 2023. Then the unprecedented attacks of the 7 October took place, which claimed 1,200 lives. Since then, over 44,000 people perished in Gaza. Entire communities have been displaced. Humanitarian needs are escalating to catastrophic levels, and hostages are still in captivity. In this context, the General Assembly has a critical role to play. The veto must be subject to greater accountability. Until meaningful reforms are achieved, This Assembly must decisively bridge the gaps left by the Council inaction and continue to urge the Council to propel stability worldwide. With great power comes great responsibility, and the permanent members of the Council cannot be exempted from such responsibility. When it comes to human suffering, we must unite in the pursuit of peace. My country emphasizes the necessity of adhering to the principles enshrined in the Pact of the Future, ensuring that multilateralism evolves to meet the expectation of those it serves.
