Colleagues, The messages we send to the world through these resolutions matter, and both of these resolutions have significant problems. One rewards Hamas and downplays the need to release the hostages, and the other denigrates Israel without providing a path forward to increasing humanitarian assistance to Palestinian civilians. For these reasons, and despite good faith efforts to find common ground, the United States will vote against these resolutions. We encourage other delegations to do the same. We can and must do better to set the region on a path toward a durable peace for the benefit of future generations of Palestinians, Israelis, and the broader region. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of United States. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Yemen.

Madam President, thank you for holding this meeting within the emergency special session of the General Assembly upon the request of the Arab Group, the OIC, and NAM. More than 400 days have elapsed since the beginning of the brutal Israeli aggression against the Gaza Strip, which has resulted in destructive results more than 44,000 Palestinian martyrs, more than 70 of them are women and children, more than 165,000 injured, in addition to thousands missing or under the rubble. The Palestinian people are facing an unprecedented humanitarian crisis, unwitnessed by humanity since World War II. 80 of the civilian infrastructure has been destroyed. Israel continues occupying power has weaponized hunger as a weapon of war Gaza is a place where the stench of death is everywhere it has become a piece of hell and the most dangerous place for children in the world it is no longer acceptable for the occupying power to continue to refuse uh the ceasefire and to continue with its brutal crimes and massacres against the Palestinian civilians in Gaza and the West Bank, the majority of whom are women and children. This is a clear violation of international humanitarian law, human rights law and all international conventions. The occupying power, Israel, believes it is above the law, and the Security Council, particularly, and the international community, is unable to put an end to its grave and brutal violations against the Palestinian people and to hold those who perpetrated those crimes accountable for them. double standards has allowed Israel to continue its killing and destruction and the crime of genocide. We have repeatedly reaffirmed that the continuation of this brutal Israeli war gives a justification for the forces of evil in the region to continue to destabilize the region and the world and to take it all towards the unknown. We reiterate our strong call to the international community and the Security Council to put an end to this humanitarian, moral and legal catastrophe against the Palestinian people, who deserve respect, dignity and justice like all other peoples. The genocide crime perpetrated by Israel against the Palestinian people and the call of its criminals to exterminate that people and to deny their right to exist as a nation constitutes a black blemish and blot on the conscience of humanity. We renew our welcome of the advisory opinion of the ICJ of 19 July on the legal consequences of the policies and the practice of Israel in the occupied Palestinian territories occupied since the 5th of June 1967. We renew our condemnation for the adoption by the Israeli entity of two laws to ban the work of UNRWA. We believe this decision to be a clear violation of international conventions. UNRWA is the blood, is a lifeline for the millions of Palestinian refugees, it is under constant attack by Israel, the occupying power, and it's undermining its operations in the occupied territories, including East Jerusalem. This illegal decision exacerbates the suffering of millions of Palestinians, threatens regional stability and the possibility of achieving peace. It is also a clear defiance of the authority, immunities and privileges of the United Nations and Israel's commitment under the Fourth Geneva Convention and the run against the international, the collective will of the international community. We reiterate our support for the UNRWA and its continued work and discharge of its irreplaceable and indispensable humanitarian role in the provision of support to the Palestinian people to avoid the catastrophe that is resulting from the use of, uh, humanitarian relief as a tool of war in a grave violation of international law. We welcome the ceasefire agreement in Lebanon. We hope that it will be complied with. We call upon the international community and the Security Council to discharge their historic and moral responsibilities and to take immediate actions to put an end to this barbaric Israeli aggression against the Palestinian people and to put an end to the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories, as well as supporting this people and providing assistance to it. This is the collective commitment of us all and a collective obligation of us all. We call upon all states to put an end to the bloodbath and to take a united position to achieve peace and the just and lasting solution to the question of Palestine. This will not be achieved until the Palestinian people exercise their inalienable legitimate rights and the establishment of their independent state on the borders of 4 June 1967 with its capital in East Jerusalem. Words are not enough. Resolutions and statements are not enough. The Security Council must discharge its responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security and take without delay a mandatory resolution for the end of the ceasefire, to save more lives and to stop the horrifying crimes against the Palestinian people. reaffirm the resolutions of the Arab and Islamic summit held recently in Riyadh. We call, we look forward to the holding of the high-level international conference for the settlement of the Palestinian question, which will be held in June of next year and will be co-facilitated by Saudi Arabia and France. We call upon peace loving people to support the draft resolutions on the ceasefire and the following the use of the veto power in the Security Council. Thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Yemen. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Guyana.

President, thank you for your swift response to the request of the chairs of the Arab Group, OIC, and the NAM Coordinating Bureau in convening the resumed 10th Emergency Special Session of the General Assembly. Three weeks ago, the Security Council met to consider a resolution tabled by its 10 elected members after five weeks of careful consultations. Disappointingly for Guyana, who had the honor of coordinating this effort, and I'm sure for many others in this assembly, those efforts did not culminate in an unequivocal demand for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, a demand which the Security Council as a whole has been unable to make after more than a year of war in Gaza. Despite the strong political will that exists for the Council to fulfill its charter mandate in response to the atrocities being committed in Gaza, the Council has been hamstrung by the use of the veto, as was once again demonstrated on 20th of November. President, A ceasefire in Gaza is the first and most fundamental step to ensure the protection of all civilians in Gaza in both the short and long term. There can be no sustainable improvement of the humanitarian situation in Gaza without a ceasefire. Neither can civilian life be safeguarded without a ceasefire. The world continues to witness the unprecedented impact of Israel's unrelenting violence in Gaza. Almost 45,000 persons have been killed and thousands more injured. Famine is likely occurring or imminent. Almost the entire population has been displaced multiple times. The healthcare system has been decimated and people are without access to reliable healthcare. All of this is compounded by the approach of winter and thousands not having access to appropriate shelter. In the context of the apocalyptic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the rapidly declining situation in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, UNRWA's role remains extremely critical. Guyana therefore deplores the decision of the Israeli Knesset to prohibit the agency's operations in Palestine from January 2025. We call on Israel not to implement this decision, but to rescind it. Guyana remains fully supportive of UNRWA's mandate decided by this General Assembly and will support the resolution tabled for adoption this afternoon. President Guyana further reiterates its call for an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire. To this end, we will also support the resolution tabled by Indonesia for adoption by this emergency special session. While the E10 resolution was ultimately vetoed, we once again stressed the need for all the Security Council members to also issue a demand for a ceasefire. Given the Council's primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security, Guyana is committed to continue engaging on all efforts to this end. President, Guyana remains deeply concerned about several extremely worrying features of Israel's unrelenting war on Gaza, which have led to entrenched suffering for the population. Allow me to highlight three of these. First, the ongoing lack of adequate humanitarian access to all parts of Gaza has had a debilitating effect on the humanitarian response. Access has steadily declined, while simultaneously growing more dangerous due in part to the breakdown of law and order in the territory. Israel continues to deny or impede requests for humanitarian access, with North Gaza suffering siege for over two months on account of this stance. Humanitarians themselves are operating in extremely challenging circumstances, with at least 343 humanitarian workers killed since 7th of October, including 253 United Nations staff. Guyana take this opportunity to remind that international humanitarian law stipulates that parties to a conflict must allow and facilitate rapid and unimpeded passage of humanitarian relief for civilians in need. Anything contrary to this is a violation of that obligation. We take note of the recent access granted to healthcare workers for interventions in North Gaza. We urge Israel to comply with its legal obligations and to allow full and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza. Secondly, the constant evacuation orders have put civilians in Gaza in an extremely precarious position. In addition to having to ensure accommodations that are far, far from ideal, civilians are also forced to grapple with severe shortages of supplies and services, severe overcrowding, and dire hygiene conditions. Guyana has taken note, for example, of the second December evacuation order issued to areas in North Canunus. As reported by OCHA, the area to which displaced civilians moved includes Al-Karrara seaport, where high tides had displaced many families in recent days. We utterly deplore the inhumanity of these constant forced movements. We call on Israel to cease this static, which has resulted in immense suffering for Palestinians who are not safe whether they move or they stay. Thirdly, the pummeling of critical infrastructure in Gaza since 7th of October 2023 has, among other things, created conditions for disease to thrive. It also ensures that recovery efforts would be made difficult, long, and expensive. The people of Palestine must have a place of redress for what has been done to them. Guyana recalls in this context the 19th of July advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice, which concluded that Israel has an obligation to provide reparation for the damage caused by its internationally wrongful acts. President, dear colleagues, the United Nations, particularly the Security Council and General Assembly, must act to bring this war to an end and to chart an irreversible path towards achieving the two-state solution. We look forward to the convening next year of the high-level international conference on the peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution. We urge all member states to participate constructively in the deliberations to secure an outcome of permanent peace for Palestine and Israel. We particularly urge Israel to abide by its international legal obligations, including its obligation to bring its continued occupation of the Palestinian territory to an end. It is clear, Madam President, after almost eight decades of war, that peace and security cannot be achieved through violence. Guyana is committed to supporting all efforts for lasting peace between Palestine and Israel. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Guyana. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Luxembourg.

Madam President, Luxembourg fully aligns itself with the statement by the EU. I will now make some comments in a personal, in a national capacity. Luxembourg would like to thank the President of the General Assembly for convening this resumed 10th Emergency Special Session. We deplore the fact that the Security Council has once again been unable to adopt a resolution calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, and this despite broad-based support from the Council's 14 members. This was due to a veto cast by the United States on the 20th of November. The veto isn't a privilege, it is a responsibility. We welcome the dogged efforts of the E10 with a view to finding an agreement the Security Council, paving the way for a lasting solution to this conflict which has gone on for too long. A common objective transcends divisions, achieving an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and an urgent improvement to access and the sustained distribution of humanitarian assistance at scale throughout the Gaza Strip, as well as an end, a lasting end to the hostilities. These fundamental principles, as per resolution 2735 of the Security Council, would have been the very heart of the resolution that was tabled, a draft resolution on which so many hopes were pinned as over five months had gone by since the last Security Council resolution on the Middle East had been adopted. In the meantime, every day the tally of human lives lost continues to grow, and the main victims are women and children. It has also underscored the dire situation of persons with disabilities. The fate of Palestinian civilians trapped in the north of the Gaza Strip is unbearable. The situation is sinking further into an abyss of despair. serious violations of international humanitarian law must end now. The longer impunity prevails, the more international humanitarian law and the Geneva Conventions will lose of their relevance. The protection of civilians and respect for international law and international humanitarian law must be upheld in all circumstances without any exception. This includes UNRWA operations and workers, UNRWA being an irreplaceable humanitarian actor, a lifeline for millions of Palestinian refugees in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem and in Gaza. UNRWA's mandate, granted by this very Assembly, transcends political contexts so as to meet the fundamental needs of refugees. Luxembourg would like to reiterate its unstinting support for UNRWA. We've decided to allocate supplementary flexible amount to UNRWA 2.6 million euros which will bring our total contribution to UNRWA for this year to roughly 10 million euros this sustainable and predictable funding aims to guarantee essential services continue to be provided to millions of Palestinian men and women who depend on UNRWA for their survival their health care and their education Luxembourg strongly deplores the Knesset's adoption of laws aiming to abolish UNRWA's activities in the occupied Palestinian territory. We urge the Israeli government to guarantee that UNRWA can continue to implement its mandate in the interest of the peace and security of all, as the Secretary-General also requested in his letter dated 9 December 2022. Without UNRWA, the humanitarian system in the occupied Palestinian territory will collapse. Without UNRWA, there cannot be food security. Without UNRWA, millions of people won't get access to basic health care. Without UNRWA, an entire generation will lose out on its right to education. Ladies and gentlemen, until we have a just and lasting political solution to the conflict, within the framework of a two-state solution, UNRWA's mandate will remain essential. For this reason, Luxembourg co-sponsored and will be voting in favor of the two draft resolutions at the General Assembly this afternoon, the first on a ceasefire in Gaza and the second on the crucial importance of safeguarding UNRWA. Luxembourg remains committed to the peaceful settlement of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, guaranteeing Israel's right to security, all the while respecting the inalienable right of Palestinians to self-determination and to live in dignity. It is only comprehensive, just and lasting peace on the basis of the two-state solution that will help to break the infernal cycle of violence. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Luxembourg. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Russian Federation.

Madam President, even against the backdrop of the dramatic events currently unfolding in Syria, it is unacceptable to forget about the horrific situation in Gaza, where Israel's military operation continues, an operation as a result of which tens of thousands of peaceful civilians have died and continue to die. Throughout the long months of this escalation, the Security Council has not taken any tangible measures so as to ensure a ceasefire in the enclave. Humanitarian decisions remain dead letter, and yet several hundred humanitarian workers have died, those who were putting their lives on the line providing assistance to Palestinians. Why did this happen? Traditional criticism Critics of the Security Council will probably say that it's due to the traditional problems plaguing this body, but such an assertion not only does not reflect the real crux of the problem, it also… means that the one UN member state which is fully responsible for the situation frees this delegation from criticism. It has blocked six Security Council decisions calling for a ceasefire, including the decision vetoed on 18 October 2023, a draft resolution tabled by Brazil, which contained an unequivocal condemnation of the 7 October attacks. And I'm saying this for the benefit of our US colleague who lamented the fact that no such Security Council decisions were tabled. Many of you pointed the finger at the Security Council as a whole, failing to name the delegation, although we all know full well that we are all referring to the United States. The latest victims of the narrow-minded decisions of the US were the E-10, the E-10's draft resolution which called for an end to the bloodshed in Gaza at last. Thus, the outgoing Democratic administration, which positions itself as a defender of human rights, a bastion of freedom, once again sided with the impunity, inhumanity, and violence. It sent the following signal to the world: if you're a close ally of the United States, well, you must abide by no laws or restrictions. Your obligations under international law, they're absolutely empty. Distinguished US colleagues, not everyone in the room today will speak openly about what they think about your veto, because many fear the consequences. We know that Washington punishes any dissent from it, not to mention any criticism of it. But do not worry. The US's unsightly role in this current crisis and in everything that's going on in the Middle East will still go down in history. Madam President, The veto is an instrument which was designed by the founding fathers of the UN not to give license to your friends to kill civilians. It was created to ensure that Security Council decisions are balanced in their character. Unfortunately, the US has not realized this and is using this to encourage the Israeli military machine. As a result, over 44,000 people have died in Gaza. How many more tens or hundreds of thousands of Palestinians will have to die for the US to open their eyes and to awaken their conscience? The ongoing Israeli military operation in Gaza, how is it helping to release the hostages, to secure their release? These hostages include Russian and US citizens. What about West Jerusalem's actions against Lebanon or its foray deep into Syria? How are they helping the situation? As they have such strong US support, as they're getting off scot-free in Gaza, Israel is launching more and more new military operations and using pan-regional instability to achieve its military objectives by force. All of this is part and parcel of a chain of events, part of which the Joe Biden administration has given carte blanche to the current administration in Israel. And this carte blanche has not managed to solve any of the problems in the situation in the Middle East. In fact, the current US administration has provoked a number of crises. 133 days have passed Palestinian women and children have died. Security Council members are forced to continue listening to US assertions about the effectiveness of their bilateral diplomacy on the ground and watch as they turn a blind eye to what's happening, what's been done by Israel. In July, Resolution 2735 was adopted. endorsing the so-called Biden plan, as you know, Russia abstained. As we warned back then, the resolution was underpinned by clear sleights of hand. West Jerusalem is not only following that plan, in fact, it continues to set more and more new conditions, which it knows are unacceptable to the other party. This document effectively provided diplomatic cover for Israel's military operation in Gaza. And there were other maneuvers that took place. For instance, Algeria's initiative, which talked about the inacceptability of an offensive on Rafah. Such spineless connivance with Israel, the US's blindness, is unacceptable. Today in the world there are hardly any people left prepared to continue to believe the US. This is clearly demonstrated by the outcome of the election of the vote on the resolution that occurred on the 20th of November. Many of the US's allies did not support its position and we will probably see more of the same as we vote on the resolutions on UNRWA and on the ceasefire this afternoon. We fully support these draft resolutions. Today, all of the UN member states have the opportunity to reassert their position in defense of the Palestinians, to protect Palestinians and UNRWA, not just in word, but in deed. We value the constructive approach of the co-sponsors. They've exhibited flexibility and a willingness to compromise. We call on everybody to vote in favor of the draft resolutions. for thousands of peaceful civilians who have lost their lives in the Middle East, we will be taking a step too late. However, it is not too late to help those who are still alive. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Russian Federation. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Costa Rica.

Madam President, since the onset of the conflict that has led to the resumption of the 31st special session of the General Assembly, Costa Rica has called for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We have urged an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire. We have emphasised that there is a need for the civilian population of Gaza to have access to basic services and the humanitarian aid vital for their very survival. Moreover, we have reaffirmed the obligation which falls upon all parties to the conflict to respect international law. This includes international humanitarian law. They are also obliged to ensure the full and unconditional implementation of Security Council Resolution 2735. All of the above was reflected in the text of the resolution presented on the 20th of November by the elected members of the Security Council. That text was driven by their deep concern at the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the need to address it urgently. Costa Rica expresses its gratitude to Guyana for its coordination work and to Algeria, Ecuador, Japan, Malta, Mozambique, the Republic of Korea, Sierra Leone, Slovenia and Switzerland for their efforts. We thank them for working in good faith to provide a legally binding obligation to end the hostilities. Moreover, the text contains a condemnation of all acts of terrorism that implicitly covers those committed by Hamas on October 7, 2023, and the taking of hostages. However, its adoption proved impossible. Madam President, the obligations pursuant to international humanitarian law are binding upon all parties to the conflict. irrespective of any inaction on the Security Council's part. Costa Rica calls upon both the Security Council and this Assembly to utilise all the tools provided by the Charter of the United Nations to respond to situations of this kind. Moreover, we reaffirm that the role played by UNRWA is essential and irreplaceable for millions of Palestinian refugees in the region, particularly in view of the current situation in Gaza. For this reason, we once again express our support for the agency, as well as for the International Court of Justice. We trust in the integrity of the institution and its officials. We also remind this General Assembly that it has the mechanisms it needs to address the gaps left by Security Council inaction and to ensure that the fundamental principles of the organization are upheld. This complementarity between the General Assembly and the Security Council is vital to preserve the legitimacy and effectiveness of the multilateral system. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Costa Rica. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Bangladesh.

Madam President, we thank you for the resumption of the plenary meeting of the tenth emergency special session of the General Assembly. Today, ruthless devastation and atrocities in Gaza continue. disregarding all calls and concerns of the international community, including the United Nations system. So many deaths and damages are unacceptable to any person of conscience. Bangladesh aligns itself with the statements delivered on behalf of the OIC group and on behalf of the non-aligned movement. Madam President, despite adopting a number of resolutions in the 10th emergency special session, we have been witnessing the continuation of one of the horrific massacres in the history of the world. We need to immediately stop the aggression, killing, and all other illegal practices in the occupied Palestinian territory by bringing an end to Israeli occupation and apartheid. Deplorably, after 7 October 2023, more than 44,000 Palestinians have been killed, and Gaza has been destroyed. Unfortunately, Israeli aggression and genocide has been intensified in other parts of the occupied Palestinian territory of the West Bank and East Jerusalem, as well as in other countries in the Middle East. The arrangement for a cessation of hostilities to bring an end to the Israeli aggression against Lebanon is an encouraging development. In this regard, we join others calling for the full implementation of resolution 1701 of 2006. Madam President, At this moment, the international community needs to take urgent immediate action to end all hostilities and illegal occupation by Israel. We commend the continuous efforts to take forward the discussion towards a peaceful solution to the question of Palestine. In this regard, we welcome the launch of the Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution. We demand full membership of the State of Palestine in the United Nations and call upon the UN Security Council to recommend the same without delay. We also echo the call of the resolution issued by the recent extraordinary Arab Islamic summit to mobilize international support to suspend Israel's participation in the UN General Assembly. Madam President, without ensuring accountability, without bringing the perpetrators to justice, peace cannot be established fully. We recall the orders of provisional measures and advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice and emphasize on ensuring full respect to those orders and their full implementation by immediately stopping Israeli attack and by full withdrawal of Israeli forces from the occupied Palestinian territory and other occupied Arab territories in the Middle East. We also refer to the indictments by the International Criminal Court and call upon all member states to assist in its implementation. Accountability must be ensured for the perpetrators of mass atrocity crimes. We also would like to welcome the decision to establish, under the auspices of the United Nations, the international mechanism to assist the investigation and prosecution of persons responsible for the most serious crimes under international law committed in the occupied Palestinian territory. Madam President, Gaza has been demolished and it could take 350 years for Gaza to rebuild if it remains under blockade. In this destroyed territory, when many dead bodies are under the rubble, when the remaining alive people are in dire need of humanitarian assistance and desperately seeking any kind of help to save life, Israel has been using forced starvation and forced displacement to continue their aggression against the innocent civilians. Regrettably, Israel has been killing and attacking the UN humanitarian personnel and destroying its facilities, and furthermore, it has passed legislation to stop UNRWA's activities. that will have devastating humanitarian consequences. Such actions against the UN humanitarian agencies are truly deplorable. We commend the role of UNRWA despite so many challenges and financial constraints, and also for maintaining humanitarian principle of neutrality. We urge to take all necessary measures to safeguard the mandate of UNRWA, save its staffs, premises and resources, and extend all kinds of support to UNRWA, including financial contribution. We also refer to the Secretary-General's proposal for an increased assessed contribution from the regular budget of the United Nations for UNRWA. Madam President, immediate ceasefire is must to save the innocent people from an unimaginable catastrophe. However, for a durable solution for peace and stability in the Middle East, Establishing a sovereign and independent Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital, based on the pre-1967 border, is a must. In this regard, we once again call for undertaking immediate necessary steps to implement the General Assembly resolution with regard to Palestine's admission to the United Nations as a full member. Finally, Madam President, we are going to consider two resolutions, and like previous resolutions of the ESS, we hope those will be adopted. We would like to see immediate and full implementation of these resolutions and full cooperation by the members of the U.N. Security Council, which is the primary responsible body for maintaining international peace and security. Bangladesh remains concerned that if the decades-old injustice against and suffering of the Palestinians are not addressed, this would continue to erode U.N. acceptance among the mass people around the globe. We must maintain sanctity and relevance of this august top multilateral body. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Bangladesh. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Spain.

Madam President, Spain aligns itself with the statement made by the European Union. We wish to make the following statement in our national capacity. Spain is grateful for the convening of this special session following the Security Council's inability to agree upon a ceasefire in Gaza on the 20th of November. That followed the use of the veto by one of its permanent members. We wish to thank the Security Council and particularly the 14 members of it who voted in favour. We thank them for their efforts to adopt a text that would stop the violence in Gaza. More than a year since the onset of the crisis, an agreement from the Security Council is all the more necessary. Spain laments the dizzyingly high number of civilian victims in Gaza. That number now exceeds 44 000 deaths since the indiscriminate terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas against Israel on 7 October. Those attacks were brutal. We have been unequivocal in our statements. The conclusion of a ceasefire agreement in Lebanon should lead to an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, a ceasefire which allows the release of hostages and the entry at scale of humanitarian aid into Gaza through all land border crossings. As such, we thank mediators for their work and we encourage them to continue. We must put an end to the violence in Gaza and usher in a new phase, a phase grounded in an international multilateral rule-based order. Moreover, it is vital to stop the action by violent violent settlers in the West Bank. That action compounds instability. We fervently support UNRWA both financially and politically. Since the 1st of July, we have chaired its advisory commission. There, we work to preserve the vital role of the agency, including in the stabilization phase. Spain repudiates the legislation passed in the Israeli parliament on the 28th of October. That legislation directly hampers UNRWA's ability to discharge its mandate, a mandate granted to it by this very General Assembly. That legislation is an absolute challenge to international law. Faced with these challenges, Spain reiterates its support for the International Criminal Court. Its work is work we defend. We reiterate the fact that we staunchly believe that international law is applicable. That includes IHL. Madam President, the stabilization in the post-conflict phase requires our immediate attention as a sign of political and financial support for the Palestinian National Authority so that it can assume its responsibilities as a unified government across all occupied palestinian territories on twenty one november we held the first intergovernmental meeting between spain and palestine. the entire international community must support the pa so that it is successful in restoring security and basic services and so that it can tackle reconstruction in gaza. President Spain has always maintained that the only solution to the conflict in Middle the Middle East is the implementation of the two-state solution Spain's recognition of the P the state of Palestine as well as the that recognition from other like-minded Partners serve to reactivate that proposal that was the driving force behind the global Alliance which was launched in New York in October it's held its first two meetings in riad and Brussels we hope that the global Alliance will produce concrete proposals so that the peace conference that the general assembly is seeking to in June can lay the foundations for regional stability. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Spain. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of United Arab Emirates.

Madam President, today we meet once again in the General Assembly to support the Palestinian cause. to ensure the protection of the equitable rights of the Palestinian people and to promote peace in the region. This has become a frequent scene since October 7 of last year. The resumed 10th emergency special session of the General Assembly was convened several times, following the Security Council's inability to adopt a resolution calling for a permanent, immediate, and comprehensive ceasefire in Gaza and its failure to fulfill its mandate of maintaining international peace and security. I align myself with the statements delivered by the Gulf Cooperation Council, the Arab Group, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, and the Non-Aligned Movement, all of which expressed the need for an urgent and immediate ceasefire. This too has been expressed by the international community over the past 14 months. I also emphasize the importance of allowing urgent access to at-scale humanitarian assistance throughout the Gaza Strip, along with the release of the hostages and detainees. We also renew our call for the protection of humanitarian workers and condemn the attacks on them. In line of the dangerous developments taking place in the occupied Palestinian territory, and most especially in the Gaza Strip, We must take a firm stance and act urgently against the continued killing of civilians and the deteriorating tragic humanitarian situation. It is shocking that the prices of basic foodstuffs in Gaza soared by more than 1000% compared to pre-war levels. This is in addition to the displacement of more than 130,000 people over the past few weeks due to the Israeli military's ongoing operations, while in the West Bank there is rising violence and accelerating settlement activities. On the other hand, the ceasefire agreement, reached between Lebanon and Israel last month gave us a glimmer of hope of a permanent ceasefire along the Blue Line and the implementation of resolution 1701. This would spare the people of Lebanon additional suffering. At the same time, The United Arab Emirates strongly condemns the Israeli forces recent seizure of the buffer zone in the Golan Heights. This is in violation of international law, particularly the agreement of disengagement signed between Israel and Syria in 1974. We stress our commitment to the unity, independence and territorial integrity of Syria, and will continue our calls for de-escalation in the region and the restoration of security and stability. Madam President, UNRWA's development and relief mandate to support and protect Palestinian refugees is extremely important. This mandate must continue until there is a permanent, just and comprehensive solution to the Palestinian cause, including the plight of the refugees and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital, based on the two-state solution. Both the General Assembly and the Security Council have an important role to play in addressing all actions aimed at undermining ONRWA's work, including the Israeli Knesset's recent decision to prohibit the work of the agency, and continue enabling the agency so that it can continue its work and perform its indispensable and irreplaceable role. In this regard, we stress the importance of the Secretary-General's message in his 9 December letter regarding the serious challenges facing the Agency and the impact of the Knesset's decisions. On the other hand, we commend the recommendations of the report of the Independent Review Group led by Catherine Colonna, and we encourage their implementation to improve the working methods of the Agency in the long term. Finally, Madam President, let us work together to end this protracted conflict and to protect the Palestinian people and all other peoples of this region from the plight of war and destruction. Let us support their aspirations of justice, security, and stability. Thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative of United Arab Emirates. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Brazil.

Madam President, we gather again today in the shadow of not just immense human suffering in the Gaza Strip, but also of repeated legal and moral failures in the Security Council. The ongoing tragedy in Gaza has demanded immediate and decisive action for over a year now. Yet the Security Council, tasked with the responsibility to act, has been repeatedly rendered impotent by the veto of just one permanent member. Indeed, the United States has yet obstructed another ceasefire resolution, yet another one that could have contributed to stopping the carnage against Palestinians, allowed humanitarian assistance in and within Gaza, enabled the unconditional release of hostages, and paved the way for real diplomatic efforts towards sustainable peace. The veto in this instance is indefensible. It sends a chilling message that the lives of Palestinian men, women and children are expendable. This is not merely a diplomatic failure. It is a betrayal of the principles upon which the United Nations was founded. The veto here continues a troubling pattern of complete disregard for Charter responsibilities by some permanent members, seriously undermining the integrity, legitimacy and effectiveness of the Security Council. Colleagues, the situation on the ground is appalling. There are reasonable grounds to believe that serious international crimes are being committed in the Gaza Strip, and yet the Security Council is prevented from acting. The recurrent veto with respect to the situation in Gaza has been enabling impunity, emboldening aggressors. This raises urgent legal and moral questions about accountability. Moreover, a deeper sense of empathy has been absent in this repeated abuse of veto power. The population in Gaza are not statistics. They are human beings with hopes, dreams and an inherent right to live in dignity in a sovereign state. Permanent members, all permanent members have an obligation over the responsible use of the veto. A moral duty stems from that responsibility. This moral duty implies standing up against injustice even when doing so may be politically or strategically costly. It implies prioritizing human lives over geopolitical considerations. clear this is not what the international community is witnessing since the first veto related to this crisis was cast during Brazil's presidency of the Security Council in October last year. How many innocent lives could have been spared if Council efforts to achieve peace were not obstructed? Madam President, as we regret the profound moral disconnection from the harsh reality in Gaza manifested in the repeated vetoes against resolutions in the Security Council, we call for the long overdue institutional and comprehensive reform of that body in order to make it more representative, legitimate and effective. Finally, in the absence of the necessary Council action for the reasons indicated before, It falls upon this General Assembly under UN Charter to take matters in its own hands, once again pertaining to the situation in Gaza. Brazil is co-sponsoring the two draft resolutions to be voted this afternoon. Both of them, besides embodying measures that enjoy virtually unanimous support, leave no room for doubt about the international community's resolve in spite of all the Security Council's failings to advance peace, accountability, and to safeguard UNRWA's indispensable role for the present and the future of the Palestinian people. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Brazil. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Thailand.

Madam President, Thailand regrets that the Security Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution proposed by Guyana as coordinator of the EATL, that would have demanded an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, as well as the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Veto is not a privilege, but a great responsibility. It should be used responsibly and with accountability to maintain international peace and security. Madam President, the situation in Gaza is too dire for the UN to remain silent. Thailand will vote in favor of the resolution demanding for peace, for ceasefire in Gaza, with the hope that it would re-energize determination to speed up the path toward peace in the region and the fulfillment of the two-state solution. We urge all parties concerned to immediately reach a ceasefire agreement and terminate all acts of hostilities, protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, comply with international humanitarian law, and implement relevant Security Council resolutions. We also repeat our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, including Thai nationals who are not involved in the conflicts, as well as their proper treatment pending their release. Madam President, Thailand reiterates our concern for the serious humanitarian, political and security risk from any interruption and suspension of UNRWA's work. The organization remains the backbone of all humanitarian response to generations of Palestinian refugees and civilians in Gaza and the wider region. We repeat that there is no alternative to UNRWA. In this regard, vote in favor of the resolution support for the mandate of the UNRWA. We also urge all member states to strengthen political and finance support to ensure its unimpeded operation and provision of services for the stability of the region as mandated, the mandate that the General Assembly have entrusted to them. Madam President, Thailand reiterates our call for all parties to fully comply with their obligations under international law and relevant Security Council resolutions. We continue to appeal to all parties to seek ways to resolve the situation through peaceful means with a view to realizing the two-state solution by which the states of Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security. I thank you, Madam President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Thailand. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Iceland.

Madam President, the fact that there is still need for us to reconvene this emergency session more than 14 months into the conflict that broke out following the heinous terrorist attacks of 7 October last year is beyond belief. The ongoing impasse in the Security Council and its continued failure in protecting the humanitarian system in Gaza, averting further escalation and civilian casualties is, to put it mildly, deeply regrettable. The violence and the suffering must stop now. A humanitarian catastrophe has unfolded before our eyes. We continue to call on Israel and Hamas to urgently agree to and implement a sustained ceasefire and commend all efforts to try to bring an agreement to fruition. While this ongoing situation continues, we, the international community, are failing close to two million civilians in Gaza every day. The people of Palestine and Israel deserve to live in peace and security. in prosperous and democratic societies. They deserve to live without fear of aggression or terrorist attacks. Iceland has friendly and full diplomatic relations with both Israel and Palestine, and we continue to call for an immediate ceasefire and a credible path towards a two-state solution. Iceland has always been and continues to be a strong supporter and advocate for international law and the international system. Iceland persistently condemns violation of international law. We demand accountability for such violations wherever they take place. Iceland has consistently condemned in the strongest possible terms the brutal and indiscriminate terrorist attacks by Hamas in October 2023. There can be no justification for terrorism. We have also repeatedly called for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. The apparent violation of international humanitarian law in the Gaza conflict are unjustifiable and must end. Too many innocent lives have been lost. Madam President, given the dire humanitarian needs since the start of the Gaza conflict, Iceland has more than doubled humanitarian assistance and other contributions to the OPT. we announced another additional contribution to UNRWA at the Gaza Ministerial Conference in Cairo on December 2nd. We would like to stress, however, that without humanitarian access, aid cannot reach those in need. Desperation, hunger, thirst, diseases, and no place of safety. These are the apocalyptic conditions that the Gaza population faces. Under these circumstances, a halt to the operations of UNRWA the most centrally placed humanitarian organization responding to the needs of Palestine refugees in the Middle East, would have devastating consequences. Furthermore, UNRWA is the main provider of education and health services to millions of Palestine refugees, and the consequential vacuum in services and humanitarian aid in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, may further destabilize the situation in these areas, in Israel and in the region, and may fundamentally jeopardize the prospects for a two-state solution. Therefore, Iceland has called for the reconsideration of the recent legislation in the Knesset that, if implemented, may prevent UNRWA from carrying out its critical operations in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza. Effectively, UNRWA will no longer be able to fulfil its mandate in the occupied Palestinian territory, a mandate given to it by this august Assembly, its parent organ. It should only be this Assembly that defines it. We are keenly aware of the importance of holding UN agencies to the highest standards. We welcome the prompt and thorough follow up action initiated by the United Nations Secretary General and the UNRWA Commissioner General following serious allegations directed towards some workers of the agency. We expect its continued implementation, including the recommendations of the Colonna report. Madam President, as I conclude, let me restate the only long term sustainable solution to this conflict, a two state solution based on international law, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security and mutual recognition. There is no better path towards peace, and the people of Palestine and Israel deserve nothing less. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Iceland. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Mauritania.

Madam President, at.

The outset, I would like to thank the President of the General Assembly for convening this resumed 10th Emergency Special Session to discuss the disastrous situation which is ongoing in the occupied Palestinian territory, the OPT. We align ourselves with this statement delivered on behalf of the Arab Group. the Organization for Islamic Cooperation, the Non-Aligned Movement as well. Madam President, we are meeting one year after the start of the brutal war on Gaza, a year of arbitrary murder which does not distinguish between civilians, women, children, the elderly, or the sick, a genocide, a genuine genocide which has cost the lives of tens of thousands of people, displacing hundreds of thousands, razing to the ground entire neighborhoods and urban areas. This genocide has gone hand in hand with Israel's war-mongering in the north of Gaza, where 500,000 civilians live in peril. They have very limited life choices. These are women, children, and the elderly. They are choosing between forced displacement, evacuation, and death. Death by starvation or death as a result of bombing and lethal weapons being deployed. This is the so-called general's plan, that is evacuate everyone from the region by bombing, refugee camps, hospitals, transforming the north of Gaza into a military zone. The international community was incapable to put an end to all this. Israel is continuing to defy international peace and security by waging war in the region. Israel is continuing to regard with contempt the decisions taken by various organizations and bodies. An irresponsible resolution, decision was adopted to ban UNRWA. in violation of the UN General Assembly's decisions, the GA being the authority, the only authority with the right to change the body's mandate. The occupying power has disregarded the ICJ's advisory opinion on Israel's illegal policies and practices in the OPT. This advisory opinion confirmed that Israel's continuing presence in the OPT is illegal and must end in the shortest possible amount of time. UN Member States should not recognize the situation resulting from Israel's illegal presence there, and Member States should not provide any aid or assistance which would demand recognition of Israel's presence in the occupied Palestinian territory. Despite all of these developments and this tragedy, we find ourselves once again back here at the General Assembly following the 20th November inability of the Security Council to adopt a decision tabled by the 10 elected members, the E10, calling for into alia an immediate permanent and unconditional ceasefire in the Gaza Strip. The catastrophic humanitarian situation stemming from Israel's actions nevertheless was met with a failure on the part of the Security Council to secure a ceasefire, to secure an end to this genocidal war. This confirms that the organization is in a state of moral crisis. This is therefore an opportunity to call for Security Council reform. a reform of the irresponsible and immoral use of the veto, and also it should be an opportunity for us to overhaul the values system which governs the decision making of the organization. How else can we explain the Security Council's failure to introduce a ceasefire at a time when thousands of defenseless civilians are dying under bombs? They're dying from starvation and illness, And this at a time when winter is beginning. Madam President, on the 27th of November, we welcomed the ceasefire in Lebanon. And we call for the immediate implementation of the agreement that was reached there. It is vital for Resolution 1701, a Security Council resolution, to be upheld. And the same applies to Lebanese sovereignty. The government of my country reiterates the need to put an end to the massacre being perpetrated by the Israelis in Gaza and to ensure humanitarian assistance is delivered without delay to those under siege. By way of conclusion, it's high time for the organization and the international community to uphold international peace and security, as well as to apply international law in the OPT. We must compel Israel to respect the ICJ opinion and to end the illegal and inhumane occupation. We call on all UN member states to respect the ICJ's advisory opinion and to stop sending weapons to Israel as well as to end any assistance that might help the occupation to continue that might result in an increase in the number of lives lost in Gaza. We call on all states who are continuing to provide weapons and ammunition to Israel to shoulder their legal and moral responsibilities vis-a-vis civilians, women, children, and the elderly who are dying as a result of Israel's war machine that has been deployed for a year now. We also call on member states to vote in favor of the two draft resolutions before us today so as to introduce a ceasefire and lend our support to UNRWA's mandate so that this Agency can continue to serve the Palestinian people and alleviate their suffering. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Mauritania. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Mauritius.

Madam President, Excellencies, the civilian population in Gaza is living in conditions that should make humanity shiver. The convening of this resumed session of the tenth emergency special session of the General Assembly is a strong signal that we are committed to alleviating their suffering and to seeking a durable solution to the ongoing conflict. Madam President, Since October 2023, following the attack on Israel, which we have condemned, the suffering endured by innocent Palestinian people, including women and children, has continued unabated. Both the General Assembly and the UN Security Council have been engaged in addressing the crisis, yet peace remains elusive. Mauritius is concerned that our failure to take the right decisions could lead to more bloodshed and untold suffering. The decisions we take today will bolster our organization, which remains the only beacon of hope for the Palestinians. Mauritius, therefore, reiterates its call for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. Mauritius also calls on Security Council members to live up to their responsibilities and to act promptly to address the escalating crisis. We urge world leaders to exert collective efforts for a just, lasting and comprehensive peace settlement. In this regard, the ceasefire in Lebanon, although fragile, remains a step in the right direction. Mauritius further welcomes the holding of the high-level international conference on the peace settlement on the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution to be held in June 2025. Madam President, as we speak, the death toll in Gaza and the West Bank has surpassed 44,000 people. Nearly the entire population has been forced and bombed out of their homes. Amidst this, UNRWA remains the backbone of humanitarian assistance. And yet, in October last, the Israeli parliament passed a legislation which will have catastrophic consequences for UNRWA's operations with no passage for its aid into Gaza. Dismantling UNRWA, so vital for the survival of millions of Palestinians, will lead to the collapse of the United Nations humanitarian response. We, as the international community, cannot remain indifferent. We must defend UNRWA's indispensable role and protect the unhindered access and sustained distribution of aid throughout Gaza, just as we must act for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Madam President, Mauritius also urges the Security Council to recommend the admission of the State of Palestine as a full member of the United Nations. Mauritius reiterates its unwavering stance for a two-state solution to the conflict based on relevant UN resolutions and international law, which envisages the establishment of an independent, viable and prosperous Palestinian state within secure and recognized borders, living in peace alongside the State of Israel. The path to peace and justice in the Middle East is clear, Madam President. It requires ending the occupation, respecting the right of Palestinians to self-determination, and establishing an independent, sovereign Palestine state. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Mauritius. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Plurinational State of Bolivia.

Thank you very much, Madam President. We thank the Presidency for once again convening the General Assembly for the resumed emergency special session to address the genocide in Palestine. We align ourselves with the statement made by the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defense of the UN Charter and that made by Uganda on behalf of the Non-Aligned Movement. We wish to add the following remarks in our national capacity. Madam President, the world is witnessing the greatest human tragedy of modern times in Palestine. According to UN agency reports, more than 44,000 lives have been cut short and more than 100,000 people have been wounded. 70% of these victims are women and children. These heart-wrenching figures are not merely statistics; they are lives that have been cut short, dreams destroyed, and devastated communities. The indiscriminate attacks in Gaza have transformed this strip of land into an open-air prison, an open-air prison in which civilians are collectively punished for a conflict, through a conflict that they did not choose. Women and children, who make up the majority of victims, bear the weight of displacement, the loss of loved ones, and the destruction of their homes. Elsewhere in Lebanon, the recent escalation of the conflict has ratcheted up human suffering. Cross-border attacks, indiscriminate shelling, and the wholesale destruction of entire communities have caused a new wave of displacement and injured persons. Bolivia is outraged to note the lack of resolve on the part of the international community, especially within the Security Council, to act unequivocally and decisively to halt this genocide perpetrated by Israel. Yet more serious is the repeated use of the veto by the United States against resolutions seeking an immediate ceasefire in both regions. That veto has eaten away at the hope of millions of people calling for peace and justice. Madam President, the veto is not only an act which expresses absolute insensitivity towards human suffering. It is also an undue use of privilege, a privilege granted as a result of one of the cruelest wars in the history of humankind. Casting the veto perpetuates occupation, violation and systematic violations of international law in Palestine and now in Lebanon. Consequently, my country firmly rejects the abuse of that veto and reiterates our appeal for a comprehensive reform of the Security Council. a reform which will ensure that this body is truly democratic and representative, that it can be a body which meets the interests of the international community as a whole, rather than furthering the interests of hegemonic powers. It is of paramount importance to restrict or entirely abolish the use of the veto in situations of mass atrocities such as war crimes and violations of IHL. Bolivia fully supports initiatives designed to limit this privilege in cases of genocide, crimes against humanity and other serious crimes. We cannot allow the veto being cast by a single member of the Security Council to paralyse collective efforts to save lives and restore human dignity. This Assembly cannot remain impassive in the face of this tragedy. We have a moral and political responsibility to act decisively and urgently. Distinguished colleagues, Madam President, the world cannot continue to stand idly by watching this tragedy unfold. Our organization was created to prevent human suffering, not to allow it. Peace is not a privilege, it is a fundamental right of all peoples. Let us not allow future generations to judge us for our passivity in the face of this atrocious genocide caused by Israel's bombs and weapons and those of its allies. Once again, we express our support for and solidarity with the Palestinian people and their right to self-determination. And once again, we recognize the fact that Palestine should exist as a free, independent and sovereign state within 1967 borders and with East Jerusalem as its capital. To conclude, we once again appeal for Palestine's admission to the General Assembly as a full-fledged member that will contribute significantly to international peace and security, just as it will to justice for a people that has historically been besieged and attacked. Bolivia once again underscores its unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people. This commitment is grounded in the principles of international law, justice, and peace. Multilateralism must be more than an empty word. It must become an effective tool with which we can address the most pressing problems of our age. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Bolivia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Sri Lanka.

Madam President, Sri Lanka welcomes the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon that was agreed on 26 November this year. However, the situation in Gaza remains grave. It is deeply alarming and unconscionable. With each passing day, it is spiraling out of control. We are deeply concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the increasing tension in the Middle East. During the 10th Emergency Special Session on 12 December 2003, the General Assembly adopted a resolution entitled Protection of Civilians and Upholding Legal and Humanitarian Obligations. The Security Council has been briefed multiple times during the last few months on the loss of life, the plight of the civilian population and the grave challenges faced by UNARWA as well as other humanitarian workers. On 26 November, 117 countries, including Sri Lanka, were signatories to a joint letter calling for the protection of UN and humanitarian personnel, international humanitarian law and the implementation of Security Council Resolution 2735. Last week, The UN spokesperson said that all bakeries in central Gaza have shut down due to severe supply shortages. Bread is a lifeline for many families in Gaza. It's often the only food they can access. Now even that is slipping out of reach. UN OCHA warned of a worsening nutrition situation across Gaza and says that out of the total number of children admitted for outpatient treatment of acute malnutrition since the beginning of 2024 this year, Two thirds were recorded in the past five months. Its nutrition partners report that between the 1st and 23rd November, more than 3,400 children were admitted for outpatient treatment of acute malnutrition. This, Madam President, is in addition to the 43,000 civilians reported killed, most of them women and children. Madam President, Sri Lanka's solidarity with the Palestinian people has been consistent. Sri Lanka recognizes the legitimate and inalienable right of the Palestinian people to statehood and support a just and comprehensive negotiated political settlement to the Palestinian issue in line with UN resolutions leading to two states living side by side based on the 1967 borders. In this context, Sri Lanka has been chairing the special committee to investigate Israeli practices affecting the human rights of the Palestinian people and other Arabs of the occupied territories for long years. We add our voice to the voices of other delegations in calling for all parties concerned to refrain from escalating the violence. We condemn all attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure and urge all parties to end the violence. We reiterate the importance of ensuring the protection of all civilians at all times in line with international humanitarian law. We also call for rapid, safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access to all in need in Gaza. and reaffirm our support for the full and immediate implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2735 and all relevant UN Security Council and UNGA resolutions calling for a comprehensive ceasefire and access to humanitarian provisions in Gaza. We appreciate the efforts that the Secretary-General has and continues to take to try to de-escalate the conflict. We stress that diplomacy remains the cornerstone of achieving peace in the Middle East, and that dialogue and negotiations based on mutual trust and in accordance with the UN Charter and international law must be pursued to achieve peace and stability in the Middle East. In this context, we reiterate our support for all efforts and initiatives that would stop the ongoing conflict, create and expand space for meaningful dialogue and negotiations, build trust and mutual understanding and promote cooperation for lasting peace in the Middle East. Finally, we appreciate the relentless work on the ground that has been and continues to be carried out by the UN and all its personnel at the risk of their lives. For these reasons, Sri Lanka will vote in favour of the two resolutions to be considered. Thank you, Madam Chairperson.

I thank the distinguished representative of Sri Lanka. We have heard the last speaker in the debate on this item for this meeting. We shall hear the remaining speakers this afternoon at 3:00 p.m. in this hall. The meeting is adjourned.
